claims.statement: For finite bipartite H, W subseteq V(H), a=alpha(H), and integer 1<=k<=a, tagged independent-set counts satisfy k*q_(k+1)<=2*(a-k)*q_k.
claims.scope: All finite bipartite simple graphs H, all vertex subsets W, and integer 1<=k<=alpha(H).
claims.reason: The deletion-extension incidence count and bipartite alpha(Q)>=|Q|/2 bound are valid at every stated rank, including terminal zero extension; a matching shows sharpness.

claims.statement: For finite bipartite G with degree-one v and integer p>=1, the high-tail guard 3p>=2alpha(G)+1 implies Delta_(p-1)(H_v)-Delta_(p-1)(R_v)<=0.
claims.scope: Finite bipartite simple G with original degree-one v and support s, H_v=G-{v,s}, R_v=G-N_G[s], integer p>=1 under the displayed guard; no residual or favorable premise.
claims.reason: The term equals q_p-q_(p-1); alpha(H_v)<=alpha(G)-1 and 3(p-1)>=2alpha(H_v) make the tagged shadow inequality sign it. The p=1 and above-degree cases vanish.

claims.statement: An eligible finite connected tree with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T)+2<=p has alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Finite connected trees with first strict negative forward difference and zero extension as defined in SEMANTIC-CONTRACT.md.
claims.reason: Alpha 4 and 5 contradict positive Delta0/Delta1; alpha 6 contradicts nonnegative Delta2 from the exact tree triple count, including n=7,8 vertex-cover cases.

claims.statement: Every finite ordinary connected tree with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T)+2<=p has nonpositive complete favorable original-leaf sum S(T,p).
claims.scope: The exact E993-INTERIOR-ALPHA-MINUS-TWO-AGGREGATE contract, strict original-rank selector, all original-leaf multiplicities, and no residual premise.
claims.reason: Eligibility forces alpha>=7, hence the high-tail guard at p=alpha-2. Every original-leaf term is nonpositive, so the exact strict-selector sum is nonpositive; an independent order-407 exact check tests shared-support multiplicity but is not universal evidence.

limitations: This is an informal proof audit and proposed disposition, not a governed Lean verification or registry award.
The order-404 replay and order-407 fresh check are finite evidence only; they cannot establish universality.
No independently admissible counterexample to the four stated claims was found.
